316194.title: Alon–Saks–Seymour conjecture
316194.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph. For disjoint nonempty sets $L,R\subseteq
V$ such that $\{u,v\}\in E$ for all $u\in L$ and $v\in
R$, write $B(L,R)=\{\{u,v\}: u\in L,\ v\in
R\}$ for the edge set of the corresponding complete bipartite subgraph of $G$.
Call $bp(G)$ the least $k$ for which there exist such pairs
$(L_1,R_1),\dots,(L_k,R_k)$ with

$$
E=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^{k} B(L_i,R_i),
$$

that is, the sets
$B(L_1,R_1),\dots,B(L_k,R_k)$ are pairwise disjoint and their union is $E$. Let
$\chi(G)$ denote the chromatic number of $G$.

Then for every finite simple graph $G$,

$$
\chi(G)\le bp(G)+1,
$$

equivalently, if $\chi(G)=k+1$ then every partition of $E$ into edge sets of
complete bipartite subgraphs of $G$ uses at least $k$ parts.
316194.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
316194.note: Refuted: Huang-Sudakov, A counterexample to the Alon-Saks-Seymour conjecture (arXiv:1002.4687; Combinatorica 2012). Abstract fetched; body not re-read.

316834.title: Weak positivity conjecture for bipartite planar graphs above three
316834.statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite planar graph, and let $P_G(q)$ denote its chromatic polynomial. **The weakened bipartite-planar positivity conjecture.**

$$
P_G(q)>0
$$

for every real $q\geq 3$.

This is explicitly presented as a weakened version of the preceding conjecture and is supported in the paper by numerical investigations; it remains open in the supplied text.
316834.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
316834.note: Weak positivity (no chromatic roots >= 3) for bipartite planar graphs, Salas-Sokal arXiv:0711.1738. Searches found no resolution; known near-counterexamples are large square-lattice strips, so no small-instance witness is expected; no finite search was run in this lane (no planar-graph generator available here).

319591.title: Coefficient-positivity conjecture for fully packed loop polynomials
319591.statement: Let $\pi$ be a matching and let $A_\pi(t)$ be its polynomial. **Coefficient-positivity conjecture.** Every coefficient of $A_\pi(t)$ is nonnegative. The conjecture is supported by computations for all matchings of size at most $8$, but remains unproved in general.
319591.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
319591.note: Fonseca-Nadeau FPL polynomial positivity, verified by the authors for matchings of size <= 8; extending the computation needs an FPL enumeration engine not built here. No search run.

320032.title: Non-revisiting Conjecture for simple polytopes
320032.statement:
Let $P$ be a simple polytope, and let $u$ and $v$ be arbitrary vertices of $P$.

**Non-revisiting Conjecture.** There is a path from $u$ to $v$ which at every step enters a different facet of $P$.

The source presents this as an equivalent formulation related to the Hirsch bound. The supplied material gives no resolution status for this formulation.
320032.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
320032.note: False: the non-revisiting conjecture for simple polytopes is equivalent to the Hirsch conjecture (Klee-Walkup), refuted by Santos (arXiv:1006.2814, Annals 2012). Abstract fetched; equivalence from standard literature, not re-read here.

320953.title: Mader's nonexistence conjecture for clique-critical graphs
320953.statement:
A $k$-connected graph $G$ is **clique-critical** if it is non-complete and $kappa(G-V(K))=kappa(G)-|V(K)|$ for every clique $K$ in $G$.

**Mader's conjecture.** There is no clique-critical $k$-connected graph.

The conjecture asks whether deleting every clique can always reduce connectivity by its order in a non-complete $k$-connected graph. The source gives no resolution evidence.
320953.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
320953.note: Kriesell survey arXiv:1101.2357 Sec.5: Mader proved nonexistence for k <= 6. Reformulation: clique-critical <=> non-complete and every maximal clique lies in a minimum vertex cut. A counterexample needs k >= 7 (large graphs); no feasible exhaustive search.

322106.title: Bousquet-Mélou–Xin conjecture on non-D-finiteness of noncrossing partition generating functions
322106.statement: Let $k$-noncrossing set partitions be set partitions whose arc diagrams contain no $k$-crossing, and let their ordinary generating function count them by size. **Bousquet-Mélou–Xin conjecture.** For every $k>3$, the generating function of $k$-noncrossing set partitions is not D-finite. The case $k=3$ is known to be D-finite, while non-D-finiteness for larger $k$ remains open.
322106.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
322106.note: Non-D-finiteness for k-noncrossing partitions (k > 3): analytic statement, no finite mechanism.

322353.title: Stones–Wanless conjecture on reduced Latin squares
322353.statement:
Let $rels(n)$ and $rols(n)$ denote the numbers of reduced even and reduced odd Latin squares of order $n$, respectively. **Stones–Wanless conjecture.**

$$
rels(n)\neq rols(n)
$$

for all positive $n$. The source presents this as another extension of the Alon–Tarsi conjecture to odd orders; no resolution status is supplied for the full statement.
322353.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
322353.note: rels(n) != rols(n): small n agree with the claim; deciding new n needs parity counts of reduced Latin squares beyond current computation. No search run.

322409.title: The conjecture on sums of distinct primes beyond the consecutive-prime bound
322409.statement: Let $s\ge 3$ be an integer, and let $p_1=2,p_2=3,\ldots$ denote the consecutive primes. **Distinct-prime sum conjecture.** Every integer $l>p_2+p_3+\cdots+p_{s+2}$ is the sum of exactly $s$ distinct primes. This conjecture proposes a sharp universal threshold for representing sufficiently large integers as sums of $s$ distinct primes; the source gives no resolution, so the claim remains open.
322409.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
322409.note: Fang-Chen Conjecture 1 (arXiv:1110.4714). Exact bitset DP: for every 3 <= s <= 200 and every l in (p_2+...+p_{s+2}, p_2+...+p_{s+2}+20000], l is a sum of exactly s distinct primes (no failure). The full statement includes Goldbach-type assertions for fixed small s, so no full proof route; no counterexample in range.

322842.title: The quasi-transitive digraph colored-kernel conjecture
322842.statement:
Let $D$ be an $m$-colored $l$-quasi-transitive digraph.

**Quasi-transitive colored-kernel conjecture.** $D$ has a $k$-colored kernel for every $k\geq l+1$.

This conjecture is motivated by the proved cases for $m$-colored quasi-transitive and $3$-quasi-transitive digraphs. Its status beyond those cases is not resolved in the supplied source.
322842.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
322842.note: k-colored kernels (arXiv:1201.2712). (1) The literal statement allows l = 1 (every digraph is 1-quasi-transitive), where the source Theorem 5 cycle is a counterexample for every k >= 2: an endpoint/domain defect, excluded as an endpoint correction (positive control reproduced, logs). (2) For l >= 2: closure cycles stay in strong components; Duchet reduces the case k = l+1 to asymmetric closure arcs at distance >= l+2. A proposed Lemma A (no far-end is a far-start) passed 300k structured samples but is FALSE in general (strong backward tournaments have unbounded diameter), so that route is closed. Random l-QT digraphs (l = 2..5, N = 8,10, 20000 samples each) and circulants (l = 4, N <= 16) gave no kernel-less closure. Still open as of Galeana-Sanchez & Tecpa-Galvan arXiv:2108.01168 (Conj. 3.15).

323763.title: Li's conjecture on the complexity of deciding k-connectivity
323763.statement: Let $k\geq 3$ be fixed, let $G$ be a graph, and let $\ell\geq 2$ be an integer. **Li's conjecture.** Deciding whether $\kappa_k(G)\geq\ell$ is $\mathcal{N}\mathcal{P}$-complete. The source states this conjecture after noting that the corresponding problem for fixed $k\geq 4$ is known and that the $k=3$ case was confirmed; it does not explicitly state a resolution for every fixed $k\geq 3$.
323763.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
323763.note: Source survey states the fixed k >= 4 case known and k = 3 confirmed, so every fixed k >= 3 is settled; nothing new remains in scope.

324248.title: Novikoff et al.'s bounded-increment conjecture for flashcard games
324248.statement:
Let $T_i(n)$ denote the first time card $i$ is seen for the $n$th time. **Novikoff et al.'s bounded-increment conjecture.** We have

$$
T_i(n+1)-T_i(n)\leq 2n
$$

for all $i$ and $n$. The paper states that this conjecture remains quite open; the preceding results establish quadratic growth but do not improve bounds on these differences.
324248.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
324248.note: Lewis-Li Conjecture 3.8 (NKS Conjecture 2) for the Slow Flashcard Game. Exact simulation (validated viewing sequence 1,2,1,2,3,1,3,...) through t = 10^8: max over all observed (i,n) of T_i(n+1)-T_i(n)-2n is 0, attained ~10^4 times. No counterexample; no proof mechanism.

325402.title: Double-Critical Hadwiger Conjecture
325402.statement: A connected graph is **double-critical $k$-chromatic** if it has chromatic number $k$ and, for every edge $uv$, deleting $u$ and $v$ lowers the chromatic number by $2$. **Double-Critical Hadwiger Conjecture.** Every double-critical $k$-chromatic graph contains a $K_k$ minor. The conjecture is proved by the cited authors for $k\leq 7$, while the case $k=8$ is open in the source.
325402.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
325402.note: Double-critical Hadwiger: known for k <= 7; hard infinite problem.

326089.title: Cover-graph incidence-poset doubling conjecture
326089.statement:
Let $P$ be a poset, let $G$ be the cover graph of $P$, and let $Q$ be the incidence poset of $G$. **Cover-graph incidence-poset doubling conjecture.** For every $t\ge1$, there exists a poset $P$ such that

$$
\dim(Q)=2\dim(P).
$$

The text notes that this holds when $t\le2$ but reports that the issue for larger values of $t$ remains unsettled.
326089.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
326089.note: MathDB statement is defective (parameter t undefined in the displayed claim); source (Trotter-Wang) question for t >= 3 is a hard dimension-theory problem. Not pursued.

328421.title: Las Vergnas's single-reorientation-class conjecture for hypercube matroids
328421.statement:
Let $C_d$ be the matroid obtained from the affine $d$-dimensional hypercube. A **single-reorientation-class conjecture** asserts that $C_d$ has a single reorientation class for every $d$.

This conjecture concerns when an oriented matroid has exactly one reorientation class. It is attributed to Las Vergnas and is known to hold for $d\leq 7$, while the general case remains open.
328421.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
328421.note: Las Vergnas hypercube single reorientation class: known for d <= 7; no tractable route.

329078.title: The two-value genus-range conjecture for chord diagrams
329078.statement:
Let $D$ be a chord diagram with $n>0$ chords. Its **genus range** is the set of genera of the thickened chord diagrams associated with $D$.

**Two-value genus-range conjecture.** If the genus range of $D$ consists of two numbers, then it is either

$$
\{0,1\}
$$

or

$$
\{1,2\}.
$$

The paper reports that this holds for all computed examples, but provides no general proof.
329078.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
329078.note: Burns-Jonoska-Saito Conjecture 3.2 (arXiv:1410.6148; JKTR 2015). Reformulated: a thickened diagram is an orientable rotation system of the cubic backbone+chords graph, so gr(D) = [gamma, gamma_M]. Exhaustive search over ALL chord diagrams with n <= 12 chords (all linear matchings, pruned by source Lemma 4.4, whose pruning was validated against unpruned runs for n <= 6): no two-value range other than {0,1},{1,2}; width-1 diagrams are exactly the 2n+2 linear forms of the known families. Implementation validated against the paper GR_n table (n <= 6) and named examples. n = 13 attempt exceeded the CPU cap (incomplete). No proof; Lean would need a topological-surface bridge.

329526.title: Kazhdan–Lusztig positivity conjecture for matroids
329526.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid, and let $P_M(t)\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be its Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial, characterized by the recursive conditions in the paper. **Kazhdan–Lusztig positivity conjecture.** For any matroid $M$, the coefficients of $P_M(t)$ are non-negative. This was proved for representable matroids using an intersection cohomology interpretation, but remains open for arbitrary matroids.
329526.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
329526.note: Proved for all matroids: Braden-Huh-Matherne-Proudfoot-Wang, Singular Hodge theory for combinatorial geometries (arXiv:2010.06088).

330337.title: Twin-pair conjecture for vertex-invariant algebraic co-rank
330337.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph, let $v\in V(G)$, and let $G-v$ denote the graph obtained by deleting $v$. **Twin-pair conjecture.** If

$$
\gamma_{\mathcal P}(G-v)=\gamma_{\mathcal P}(G)\quad\text{for all }v\in V(G),
$$

then $G$ has at least one pair of twin vertices. This is proposed as a stronger variant of the twin-free lower-bound conjecture and remains open.
330337.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
330337.note: Alfaro-Corrales-Valencia Conjecture 2.21 (arXiv:1504.06257). Requires deciding triviality of critical ideals over Z (strong Groebner bases over Z); no CAS available here. Note: with the convention gamma(empty)=0, K1 satisfies the hypothesis vacuously (an edge-case formulation defect, not significant).

332847.title: Minuscule distributive-lattice mCDE conjecture
332847.statement:
Let $P$ be a minuscule poset, and let $J(P)$ denote its distributive lattice of order ideals.

**Minuscule mCDE conjecture.** The distributive lattice $J(P)$ is mCDE.

The preceding theorem establishes the weaker CDE property for $J(P)$, and the paper reports that all classified minuscule cases checked are in fact mCDE. The conjecture asks for this stronger property for every minuscule poset.
332847.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
332847.note: Resolved: Hopkins, The CDE property for minuscule lattices (arXiv:1606.06248), Sec. 2 and 5: minuscule lattices are tCDE, and the CDE/mCDE distributions are toggle-symmetric, so mCDE follows.

333295.title: Non-expansion conjecture for bounded-degree graphs with nonnegative Bakry–Émery curvature
333295.statement: Let $d\in{\mathbb N}$. **Non-expansion conjecture.** No infinite family of finite, increasing, $d$-regular graphs satisfying $CD(0,\infty)$ can be a family of expander graphs. This is stated as a direct consequence of the preceding polynomial volume-growth conjecture, since increasing regular graphs with uniformly bounded polynomial volume growth should have Cheeger constants tending to zero.
333295.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
333295.note: Resolved: Salez, Sparse expanders have negative curvature (arXiv:2101.08242, GAFA 2022): the same approach applies to CD(0,infinity), settling the Cushing-Liu-Peyerimhoff conjecture (the source arXiv:1606.01496).

334207.title: Existence conjecture for even-dimension linear MDS $b$-symbol codes
334207.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let $b\ge 2$, and let $n\ge 2b$. A linear MDS $(n,2b)_q$ $b$-symbol code should exist.

This conjecture follows the constructions and conclusions discussed in the source's preceding subsection and proposes existence for every length at least $2b$. The source provides no proof or resolution in the supplied text.
334207.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
334207.note: CANDIDATE. Ding-Zhang-Ge Conjecture 2 (arXiv:1609.09236 p.15). New proof for every prime power q, b >= 2, n >= 2b: (i) a linear [n,n-b] code has d_b >= 2b iff every b cyclically consecutive parity-check columns are independent; (ii) such cyclic window sequences exist for every n >= b over every field, by strong induction on b via a bridge lemma (Euclid-like recursion (b,n) -> (n mod b, b + n mod b)); (iii) |C| = q^(n-b) and an explicit codeword gives d_b = 2b. See BSYMBOL-ORDINARY-PROOF.md. Diagnostics: 4106 windows have det +-1 over Z; 68 codes enumerated over F_2, F_3, F_5. Prior-art search bounded (see proof file). See LEAN-PACKET-334207.md and verification.json.

334241.title: The oriented-cycle minimum-out-degree conjecture
334241.statement: Let $C$ be an oriented cycle, and let $|V(C)|$ denote its order. **Oriented-cycle conjecture.** Every digraph $D$ with $\delta^+(D)\geq 2k-1$ contains a subdivision of any oriented cycle of order $k$. Equivalently, the source conjectures the upper bound $\operatorname{mader}_{\delta^+}(C)\leq 2|V(C)|-1$ for every oriented cycle $C$; the source does not give a resolution.

334656.title: Differentiability conjecture for Karpelevič arcs
334656.statement: Let a **K-arc** be an arc in the Karpelevič region, and let $n$ denote its order. **Differentiability conjecture.** All K-arcs of order $n$ are differentiable for every $n$. The paper notes that many, but not all, arcs are known to be differentiable, and presents the assertion as being motivated by empirical evidence; its general status is not resolved here.
334656.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
334656.note: Karpelevic arc differentiability: analytic. Possible lead not read: Bara (LAA 2020) "Proofs of conjectures on the Karpelevich arcs" (could resolve it; unverified).

335127.title: Conjecture A on semi-convergence for Artin–Tits monoids
335127.statement: Let $M$ be an Artin–Tits monoid, and let $\mathcal{R}$-reduction be the reduction system on multifractions associated with $M$. **Conjecture A.** $\mathcal{R}$-reduction is semi-convergent for every Artin–Tits monoid. The conjecture is known for every Artin–Tits monoid of FC type, while the remaining cases are open.
335127.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
335127.note: Artin-Tits semi-convergence (Dehornoy-Holt-Rees): hard; no finite mechanism.

336155.title: The $2n$-conjecture over the rationals
336155.statement: Let $S$ be an $n\times n$ zero-nonzero pattern that is spectrally arbitrary with respect to $\mathbb{Q}$. **The $2n$-conjecture over the rationals.** Then $S$ has at least $2n$ nonzero elements. The analogous bound fails over $\mathbb{C}$ but remains open over $\mathbb{R}$; the rational case is presented as a conjecture believed to be within reach.
336155.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
336155.note: 2n-conjecture over Q (Shitov): hard; no finite mechanism tried.

337337.title: Alkauskas's divisibility conjecture for binary partitions
337337.statement: Let $b_{2}(n)$ denote the number of binary partitions of $n$. **Alkauskas's conjecture.** For every $h\in\mathbb{N}$ with $8\nmid h$, there exist infinitely many $n$ such that $h$ divides $b_{2}(n)$. The conjecture is presented as an open problem concerning divisibility values of the binary partition sequence.
337337.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
337337.note: Alkauskas conjecture: verified for h <= 14 in the literature; general infinitude statement open; no mechanism.

338400.title: Gedeon–Proudfoot–Young negative-root conjecture for matroid Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
338400.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid, and let $P_M(t)$ denote its Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial. **Gedeon–Proudfoot–Young's conjecture.** The polynomial $P_M(t)$ has only negative zeros for every matroid $M$. The conjecture is known for uniform matroids of rank $n-1$ on $n$ elements, and this paper proves it for fan matroids, wheel matroids, and whirl matroids; it remains open for arbitrary matroids.
338400.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
338400.note: Real (negative) rootedness of matroid KL polynomials: open; no matroid database/engine here; no search run.

339281.title: Gu et al.'s vertex-transitivity conjecture for Dcell networks
339281.statement: Let $D_{k,n}$ be the data center network Dcell, with $k\geq0$ and $n\geq2$. **Gu et al.'s vertex-transitivity conjecture.** $D_{k,n}$ is vertex-transitive for all $k\geq0$ and $n\geq2$. The conjecture is false: the paper proves vertex-transitivity for $k\leq1$ and $n\geq2$, but proves that $D_{k,n}$ is not vertex-transitive for all $k\geq2$ and $n\geq2$.

340097.title: The Billera–Lee upper-bound conjecture for triangulated spheres
340097.statement:
Let $S$ be a triangulated $d$-sphere, and let $T$ be the Billera–Lee $d$-sphere with $f$-vector $f(S)$.

**Billera–Lee upper-bound conjecture.** For every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq d$,

$$
\tau_i(S) \leq \tau_i(T).
$$

This conjecture proposes that Billera–Lee spheres maximize the entire $\tau$-vector among triangulated spheres with a fixed $f$-vector. The source does not state a resolution.
340097.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
340097.note: Billera-Lee tau-vector maximality: hard topological-combinatorial statement; no route.

341374.title: Vignesh et al.'s total coloring conjecture for line graphs of complete graphs
341374.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, let $L(K_n)$ be its line graph, and let $\chi”$ denote total chromatic number. **Vignesh et al.'s conjecture.** For every complete graph $K_n$,

$$
\chi”(L(K_n))=2n-3.
$$

The claim extends the directly verified cases $n\leq4$ and predicts that every line graph of a complete graph is type-I. The supplied text gives no resolution.
341374.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
341374.note: Vignesh-Geetha-Somasundaram conjecture chi"(L(K_n)) = 2n-3 (survey arXiv:1812.05833 Conj. 3). Verified type 1 for 2 <= n <= 13 (CaDiCaL models independently checked; n = 12, 13 via a Z_n-equivariant ansatz). Reformulation: a type-1 total colouring = partition of all P3s of K_n into 2n-3 P3-decompositions of K_n minus matchings that partition E(K_n). Uniform cyclic ansatz fails for n = 6, 7; a 1-factorization-based framework fails for n = 6, 7. No general construction; not known resolved (only conformability, 2023).

341386.title: The $\Omega(n^{4/3})$ line conjecture for graphs
341386.statement: Let $G$ be a finite graph with $n=|V(G)|$, and call a line **universal** if it contains all vertices of $G$. **Line-count conjecture.** Every graph $G$ without a universal line has $\Omega(n^{4/3})$ distinct lines. The conjecture is known for graphs of bounded diameter and for graphs in which no line contains another, but remains open for arbitrary graphs.
341386.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found

341906.title: Balog–Shakan conjecture on sums of a set and its dilate
341906.statement:
Let $d,q$ be natural numbers with $q>1$, and let $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d$ be a finite $d$-dimensional set.

**Balog–Shakan conjecture.** One has

$$
|A+q\cdot A|\geq(q+2d-1)|A|-O_{q,d}(1).
$$

This conjecture extends the bound proved by Balog and Shakan in dimensions $2$ and $3$; the paper presents it as an assertion for all dimensions.
341906.history_check: grep of campaign prose/reviews/results/ledgers (history-matches.txt): only the r78 reservation itself and unrelated numeric/title noise; no prior disposition found
341906.note: Balog-Shakan conjecture: Mudgal (arXiv:1902.07665) proves it with O(|A|^(1-delta)) error; the exact O(1) error is an asymptotic statement with no finite mechanism.

342130.title: Finiteness conjecture for density-critical matroids of prescribed density
342130.statement: For a matroid $M$, let $d(M)$ be its density, and call $M$ **density-critical** when every proper minor $N$ satisfies $d(N)<d(M)$. **Finiteness conjecture.** For every $t\geq 0$, there are finitely many density-critical matroids with density exactly $t$. This is presented as a weakening of the conjecture asserting finiteness of $t$-density-critical matroids, and remains open.

342205.title: Bóna's upper-bound conjecture for $t$-stack-sortable permutations
342205.statement:
Let $W_t(n)$ denote the number of $t$-stack-sortable permutations of length $n$, for integers $n,t\geq 1$. **Bóna's upper-bound conjecture.** For all $n,t\geq 1$, we have

$$
W_t(n)\leq{(t+1)n\choose n}.
$$

This is one of Bóna's conjectures concerning enumeration of iterated stack-sortable permutations; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.

342771.title: The $K_5$ conjecture for $\phi^4$ prime ancestors
342771.statement:
A $\phi^4$ prime ancestor is a prime ancestor arising in $\phi^4$ theory, and $c_2^{(q)}(G)$ is its $c_2$-invariant at the prime power $q$. **The $K_5$ conjecture.** The only $\phi^4$ prime ancestor with

$$
c_2^{(q)}\equiv-1\mod q
$$

for all $q$ is the complete graph $K_5$. This was verified computationally in the ranges reported in the paper, but the unrestricted assertion remains open.

343064.title: Odd-path local antimagic total chromatic number conjecture
343064.statement:
Let $P_n$ be the path of order $n\geq 2$, and let $\chi_{lat}(P_n)$ denote its local antimagic total chromatic number. **Odd-path conjecture.** For odd $n\geq 3$,

$$
\chi_{lat}(P_n)=2.
$$

The source verifies the assertion explicitly for $n=3,5,7$ and states it for all odd $n\geq 3$; no general proof or resolution is supplied in the provided text.

343064.note: Resolved: chi_lat(P_n) = 2 for all n >= 2 except P4 (Lau arXiv:2407.14113 Thm 1.3; also Thm 3.14 in the current version of the source arXiv:1906.10332), covering all odd n >= 3.

343453.title: Benson exponent conjecture for six-cycle matrices
343453.statement:
Let $A$ be a zero-one matrix corresponding to a cycle of length $6$. **Six-cycle exponent conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{ex}(n,A)=\Theta\bigl(n^{\frac{4}{3}}\bigr).
$$

For every such matrix, the paper gives a lower bound $\Omega(n^{4/3})$ and an upper bound $O(n^{3/2})$, so the conjecture asks to close this gap. It was also investigated by Gyárfás, Keszegh, Martin, Tomon, Tardos, and Valtr.

343946.title: The general-graph rainbow matching conjecture
343946.statement:
Let $f_{\mathcal G}(n,m)$ denote the least number of $n$-element matchings in an arbitrary graph that guarantees a rainbow matching of size $m$. **Rainbow matching conjecture.**

$$
f_{\mathcal G}(n,n)=2n,
$$

and, for odd $n$,

$$
f_{\mathcal G}(n,n)=2n-1.
$$

This was conjectured based on examples for general graphs; the stated bounds distinguish even and odd values of $n$.

345108.title: Divisibility conjecture for evaluations of monomials times powers of 1+x
345108.statement:
Let $\rho$ be the evaluation map used in the paper, and let $i,j$ be nonnegative integers. **Divisibility conjecture.** For every $i,j$, the number $\rho(x^i(1+x)^j)$ is divisible by

$$
2^{\lfloor j/2 \rfloor}.
$$

The property is clear when $j$ is odd, but the even case remains unproved; this divisibility would allow the normalized matrices introduced afterward to be defined integrally.

345633.title: Cordovil–Las Vergnas connectivity conjecture for oriented matroid mutation graphs
345633.statement: For positive integers $r$ and $n$, let $\mathcal{G}^{n,r}$ be the mutation graph of uniform oriented matroids of rank $r$ on $n$ elements. **Cordovil–Las Vergnas conjecture.** For all $r,n$, the graph $\mathcal{G}^{n,r}$ is connected. The source records this as an open question and notes that it belongs to a hierarchy of three open questions.

345748.title: The list 1-2-3 Conjecture
345748.statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph with at least two edges, and assign to each edge $e$ a list $L(e)$ of allowable real numbers. A decoration is **cool** if the sums at adjacent vertices are different. **The list 1-2-3 Conjecture.** Every connected graph with at least two edges has a cool edge decoration from arbitrary lists of size three. This strengthens the 1-2-3 Conjecture and remains open.
